title: Session Cookie Authentication
subtitle: The classic form login: a POST establishes a server-side session, and an opaque HttpOnly cookie is replayed on every later request. Step through it and read each hop in the Network tab.

steps.label: Navigate to /login
steps.lede: The user opens the login page. Nothing proves who they are yet — the goal of this flow is to establish a server-side session.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log so the login redirect isn't cleared, and filter on Doc / Fetch.

steps.label: GET /login → anonymous session
steps.lede: The server returns the login form and plants a pre-auth (anonymous) session cookie plus a CSRF token embedded in the form.
steps.devtools: In the Response Headers note Set-Cookie: sid=PRE_AUTH_…. Because it is HttpOnly you will not see it via document.cookie — only here and in Application → Cookies. Remember this pre-auth value; it should change at login.

steps.label: Enter username + password
steps.lede: The user types their credentials into the form. These are posted to the app itself — there is no external IdP in this pattern.
steps.devtools: Not a network event yet. The form also carries the hidden csrf_token the server planted on the previous response.

steps.label: POST /login (credentials + CSRF)
steps.lede: The browser submits the credentials and CSRF token. On success the server destroys the anonymous session and issues a rotated session ID — the session-fixation defense.

headers: sid=s%3AsynthSESSION9f8e7d6c5b4a3210; Path=/; Max-Age=1800; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

jwt.title: Set-Cookie attributes (post-login sid)
payload: Opaque reference into the server's session store — NOT a token with claims. %3A decodes to ':' (signed-cookie prefix)
Cookie sent for the whole site
Not readable from JavaScript — blunts XSS theft
Not sent on most cross-site requests — first-line CSRF defense

steps.devtools: Open the Payload tab to see username, password, csrf_token. Then compare the new Set-Cookie: sid= against the pre-auth value: it changes. That rotation kills any sid an attacker planted (session fixation).

steps.label: GET /api/me (Cookie replayed)
steps.lede: On every following request the browser automatically replays the session cookie. The opaque sid is the sole proof of identity; the server looks it up in its session store.
steps.devtools: In Request Headers read Cookie: sid=… — the browser attached it for you. There is no Authorization header and no token; identity is entirely the server-side lookup of this opaque id. Deleting the store record revokes access instantly.

steps.label: Session established
steps.lede: The authenticated UI renders. State-changing POSTs from here carry the CSRF token (form field or X-CSRF-Token header) in addition to the cookie.
steps.devtools: Nothing more on the wire for sign-in. Inspect the live cookie and its flags under Application → Storage → Cookies. A POST /logout would return Set-Cookie: sid=; Max-Age=0 and delete the store record, so replaying the old sid afterward fails.
